land.text: the Belgorod Razriad frontier lands of the Tsardom, from which Sloboda Ukraine 'developed'

predecessors.note: Infobox predecessor: Belgorod Razriad. Cliopatria's Tsardom of Russia shape does not cover this land in these years (no common cell with the Sloboda Ukraine shape in 1700).

land.text: the Sloboda Ukraine Governorate: 'In 1765, it was converted into the Sloboda Ukraine Governorate'

successors.note: Regiments disbanded and Cossack privileges abolished by decree of 28 July 1765; the governorate became the Kharkov Viceroyalty in 1780 and the province was abolished in 1835 (Kharkov Governorate, most of the territory).

capitals.name: Sumy
capitals.note: The page says only 'the Sloboda Ukraine Cossack capital was located in Sumy until 1743'; the start year is the dossier's.

capitals.name: Kharkiv
capitals.note: Infobox capital Kharkiv; the page does not date the move beyond 'until 1743' for Sumy.

correction.text: the 1670 outline carried back to 1650 unchanged: the page gives no extent for these years, only that 'From 1650 to 1765, the territory referred to as Sloboda Ukraine became increasingly organized'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1670. The page dates the organisation of the Cossack regiments from 1650 and the colonisation waves of the 1620s-1630s ('largely in the form of Ukrainian Cossack regiments') and after the 1637-1638 Ostryanyn uprising, but names no boundary; the region was settled progressively, so the 1650s outline was probably smaller than 1670's. Extent is the researcher's bridge (confidence 1).

98,599 km2 (408 cells); the infobox gives no area. The page lists the parts as Kharkiv, Luhansk, Sumy, Belgorod, Voronezh, Kursk (and Donetsk in the infobox); the shape covers 103 of Kharkiv's 135 cells, 112 of Voronezh's 208, 71 of Belgorod's 117, 53 of Luhansk's 108, 42 of Sumy's 104 and 15 of Kursk's 123, with 5 in Donetsk and 6 in Poltava, and contains the cells of all five regimental centres (Ostrogozhsk, Kharkiv, Okhtyrka, Sumy, Izium); the city of Belgorod itself lies outside. It is a region inside the Tsardom: 'Starting from 1688, administrative control over Sloboda Ukraine belonged to Greater Russian prikaz', and the Cossacks 'were under the sovereignty of Russian tsars'. Cliopatria's Tsardom shape leaves it out, so the drawn tint is the only claim on the land.

98,140 km2 against 98,599: three cells drop out and two are added on the western edge (34.1-36.1 E, 49.2-51.0 N), under 0.5% of the area. The page's Slavo-Serbia ('From 1753 to 1764, the imperial territory of Slavo-Serbia existed to the south') lies south of the shape, so it does not explain the change; treated as outline jitter.

correction.text: shape unchanged; the years end in 1765, not 1768: 'In 1765, it was converted into the Sloboda Ukraine Governorate' and the regiments were disbanded by the decree of 28 July 1765

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria keeps the row to 1768. After the 1765 decree the land is an ordinary governorate of the Russian Empire (Kharkov Viceroyalty from 1780, abolished 1835), so the colony tint ends in 1765 and the Russian Empire's own shape should cover it from 1766.

region.text: the south-western frontier lands of the Tsardom that developed from the Belgorod Razriad, settled by Ukrainian Cossack regiments

ledger.note: 1650: Sloboda Ukraine begins to be organised as a Cossack frontier region under the tsar. 'From 1650 to 1765, the territory referred to as Sloboda Ukraine became increasingly organized' along Cossack military lines; the page dates no founding, and the extent is the Cliopatria 1670 outline.
1743: the Cossack capital leaves Sumy for Kharkiv. 'the Sloboda Ukraine Cossack capital was located in Sumy until 1743'; the infobox capital is Kharkiv.

region.text: the Sloboda Cossack regiments' lands, converted into the Sloboda Ukraine Governorate

ledger.note: 1765: the Sloboda Cossack autonomy ends. 'In 1765, it was converted into the Sloboda Ukraine Governorate'; Cossack privileges were abolished and the regiments disbanded by the decree of July 28, 1765.

certainty.note: The page gives only the modern oblasts that cover the region, no boundary and no area; the southern steppe frontier was open to the Wild Fields, and the Izium and Belgorod lines are not dated here.

notes:
Written for batch eu-16-i from two pages (budget 1-2); both are thin: neither gives an area, a boundary, or the founding year of any regiment, so the 1670, 1752 and 1763 outlines are Cliopatria's with the extent unverified.
ONE STATE OR TWO? Sloboda Ukraine (1670-1768) and Ukraine (1992-2024) share Wikidata Q598570 in Cliopatria's table (data/README.md, 'Q598570: Sloboda Ukraine / Ukraine'). They are different states: Sloboda Ukraine is a Cossack frontier region of the Tsardom and then a Russian governorate, the Ukraine row is the post-1991 republic (590,177 km2). The shared id is a Cliopatria fault; the id Q598570 is kept here as Cliopatria gives it. The Ukraine row belongs to another group; do not merge.
TYPE: written as type colony (a dependency ruled from elsewhere, drawn as a vassal tint of the metropole): the infobox calls it a 'semiautonomous region, then a province', the Cossacks 'were under the sovereignty of Russian tsars' and from 1688 it was administered by a Great Russian prikaz. Change to state if the colour agent prefers its own hue.
DATES: start 1650 (the page's 'From 1650 to 1765 ... increasingly organized'; Cliopatria starts 1670) and end 1765, month 7 (decree of 28 July 1765; Cliopatria ends 1768). The 1650-1669 keyframe carries the 1670 outline back at confidence 1. The tint after 1765 is the Sloboda Ukraine Governorate (Kharkov Viceroyalty 1780, abolished 1835), which the Russian Empire dossier (eu-17) should cover as ordinary territory.
WARS: none is named for these years on the pages opened. The only dated clash is the Tatar raid of 1591 that reached the Moscow region and led to the forts of Belgorod and Oskol (1593); the Crimean and Nogai raids were annual along the Muravsky and Izyum trails but undated, so no war entry is made (it would fall before the dossier's 1650 start).
NOT SETTLED: the Tsardom of Russia's own dossier should say whether it counts this land (Cliopatria's Tsardom shape has no cell in common with this one); the Izium line, the Belgorod Line dates and the regiments' founding years (Kharkiv, Sumy, Okhtyrka, Izium, Ostrogozhsk) need a page the budget did not allow ('Belgorod Defense Line', 'Sloboda Cossack regiments'). Slavo-Serbia (1753-1764, 'to the south' on the page) belongs with the New Serbia dossier.
